Grady County by the numbers

What does the Grady County Clerk do?

The Grady County Clerk is the county's recorder, the office that files warranty deeds, mortgages and oil and gas leases. The same office also runs the county's accounts payable, payroll and purchasing, according to the county website.

For a home sale, the clerk is where the deed ends up after closing. Until it is recorded, the public record still shows the old owner. The Grady County Courthouse in Chickasha is itself on the National Register of Historic Places.

Records are available online through OKCountyRecords.com, though certain fees apply there, and the clerk's FAQ says land records are computerized from 1929 to the present.

What does it cost to record a deed in Grady County?

Recording costs $18 for the first page and $2 for each page after that, per document. The $18 is made up of $8 for recording and a $10 preservation fee.

ItemFee
First page, conforming document$18 ($8 plus $10 preservation)
Each additional page$2
First page, non-conforming document$25, plus $10 preservation
Each additional page, non-conforming$10
Copy$1 per page
Certified copy$1 per document
Documentary stamps$1.50 per $1,000

The office takes cash and checks if you give a correct address and current phone number. It does not take temporary checks.

What makes a document conforming?

A conforming document has a 2-inch margin at the top and 1-inch margins on the other three sides, and it is legible in dark print. If the page fails that test, the fee jumps from $18 to $25 on the first page and from $2 to $10 on each added page.

Two other filing rules trip up sellers:

  • The clerk needs an original with original signatures that has been notarized, or a certified copy of an original.
  • A certified copy is stamped and sealed, and nothing can be added to it and refiled.

If a title company prepares the deed, it normally handles format. Owners who draft their own deeds for a family transfer or a quick sale are the ones most likely to pay the higher rate.

How does documentary stamp tax work in Grady County?

Documentary stamps are due on any deed where money or other consideration changes hands. The Grady County clerk charges $1.50 per thousand dollars, and a chart in the office shows common amounts.

That figure matches the statute. Under 68 O.S. 3201, the tax is 75 cents for each $500 of consideration, or any fractional part, when the amount exceeds $100. The tax is limited to conveyances of realty sold. Every instrument filed has to either pay the stamps or show its exemption on the face of the document.

The clerk also recommends attaching a bill of sale or a contract as proof of the price. As an example of the arithmetic, a $200,000 sale at $1.50 per thousand comes to $300.

How fast does the Grady County Clerk file a document?

Documents brought in between 8 am and 4 pm are filed that day, and anything presented after 4 pm is filed the next day. Returning the document to you takes seven to ten days.

The office scans every document and does not keep the original. Because of storage limits it stopped making shelf books at Book 4000, but all images are held online and backed up two ways. If you need a document right away, ask for a certified copy once it is filed, or use the online index.

  • Bring the full legal description.
  • Bring the closing statement for the stamp calculation.
  • Ask whether a veteran's DD-214 is needed in the same visit, since those are filed in the clerk's office too.

DD-214 military records are not public. They are open only to the veteran, a spouse, children, the Veterans Administration or a court order.

What is the history behind Grady County's land records?

Grady County was organized in 1907 at statehood, and Chickasha was named its seat. Before that, most of the future county belonged to the Chickasaw Nation's Pickens County, and the western edge lay in reservations opened to non-Indian settlement in 1901.

The 1898 Curtis Act ended the Chickasaw government's authority and the allotment process turned communal land into individual parcels. Those allotments are the start of many deed chains in the county. A title search on an older farm may run back to an allottee rather than a land patent.

Railroads laid out many of the towns. The Rock Island built to Minco in 1890 and reached Texas in 1892, creating Chickasha, Ninnekah and Rush Springs. The Oklahoma City and Western line created Tuttle and Amber around 1901 and 1902.

How does a cash sale reach the Grady County Clerk?

A cash sale follows the same recording path as any other sale, only with fewer lender steps ahead of it. Once the buyer and seller sign, the deed goes to the clerk with proof of price and payment of the stamps.

  1. Confirm the legal description against your last recorded deed.
  2. Sign the deed in front of a notary, since the clerk needs a notarized original.
  3. Attach a closing statement, bill of sale or contract as proof of price.
  4. Calculate documentary stamps at $1.50 per thousand, or state the exemption on the deed.
  5. Deliver the deed by 4 pm to have it filed the same day.

Grady County has about 110,000 head of cattle, a large dairy and wheat on over a hundred thousand acres by the state encyclopedia's 2000 figures, so many deeds describe ranch or farm tracts. Those descriptions run longer than a town lot and can push a deed past one page, which adds $2 for each extra page.

What local places show up in Grady County deeds?

Deeds here refer to towns, rivers and old trails. The county is bordered on the north by the Canadian River, and the Washita River crosses the middle.

  • Chickasha, the county seat, with a Rock Island Depot and a downtown historic district on the National Register.
  • Minco, home to a listed armory.
  • Pocasset, where a listed gymnasium stands.
  • Verden, once called Cottonwood Grove, where the 1865 Camp Napoleon Compact was signed.
  • Rush Springs, Tuttle, Bridge Creek, Amber, Ninnekah, Norge, Alex and Bradley.

Chickasha has also been the county's industrial leader. The Oklahoma College for Women opened there after the legislature placed it in the city, and it later became the University of Science and Arts of Oklahoma.

What should Grady County sellers know before recording?

Start by making sure the legal description on the deed matches the one in your last recorded deed. A typo can mean a corrective deed and a second recording fee.

The 2019 to 2023 Census Bureau survey counts 23,332 housing units in the county and a median build year of 1981. Many sales involve older houses and acreage, so it is worth checking that your own deed was recorded before you sell. Fixing any gap before closing speeds things up.

Property tax is a separate office. The Grady County Treasurer collects the tax, so request the balance from that office before the closing date.

More questions about Grady County, OK County Clerk

How much does the Grady County Clerk charge to record a deed?

The charge is $18 for the first page and $2 for each additional page. That includes an $8 recording fee and a $10 preservation fee. A non-conforming document costs $25 for the first page and $10 for each additional page, plus the $10 preservation fee.

What is the documentary stamp rate in Grady County?

The clerk charges $1.50 per thousand dollars of consideration, equal to 75 cents per $500 under 68 O.S. 3201. It applies when the price is more than $100, and every deed must pay it or state its exemption.

Can I record a copy of a deed in Grady County?

Only an original with original signatures that has been notarized, or a certified copy of an original, can be filed. A plain photocopy is not accepted.

How long until I get my recorded deed back?

Expect seven to ten days. Documents delivered by 4 pm are filed that day, and later ones are filed the next day.

Mcclain County by the numbers

Where is McClain County, Oklahoma?

McClain County is in central Oklahoma, about 580 square miles of land and water, with Purcell as the county seat. Cleveland County and part of Pottawatomie County lie to the north, Pontotoc to the east, Garvin to the south and Grady to the west, per the Oklahoma Historical Society.

The South Canadian River forms the northern border, and the Washita River flows near the southwestern corner. The west is hilly and was once covered in blackjack oak, while the southeastern arm is level lowland. Incorporated towns, as of 2010, were Blanchard, Byars, Cole, Dibble, Goldsby, Newcastle, Rosedale, Washington, Wayne and Purcell.

What does the McClain County Clerk do?

The McClain County Clerk is the registrar of deeds for the county and is one of eight elected officials. The clerk's page lists deeds, mortgages, plats, mineral interests, liens, court judgments, tax liens, oil and gas leases, powers of attorney and trust agreements among the records kept.

The office is at 121 North 2nd Avenue in Purcell, with a mailing address of PO Box 629, Purcell, OK 73080. Land records can be reached at 405-527-3360, and hours are 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM. The clerk also serves as secretary to the Board of County Commissioners, the Excise Board, the Tax Roll Correction Board and the Equalization Board.

Military discharge records on a DD-214 are recorded free for veterans.

What does recording a deed cost in McClain County?

The standard rate is $18.00 for the first page, which includes $8.00 for recording and $10.00 for preservation, plus $2.00 for each added page. A document that misses the statutory format rules costs more.

ItemFee
First page, standard$18.00
Each additional page$2.00
First page, non-conforming$25.00 plus $10.00 preservation
Each additional page, non-conforming$10.00
Plat of one block or less$10.00
Plat of more than one block$25.00
Certifying a copy, per page$1.00
Mechanics or materialmen's lien$10.00

The fee table cites 28 O.S. 32, and nonconforming documents are tied to subsection C of 19 O.S. 298. Mortgage recording and re-filing may involve fees payable to the County Treasurer, so call that office if you are recording a mortgage.

How is documentary stamp tax calculated in McClain County?

The clerk applies $0.75 for each $500 of the purchase price, rounding up to the next $500, and it applies only when the price exceeds $100. The county site has a calculator that does the rounding for you.

Proof of price must come with the deed. A closing statement, a notarized bill of sale or an affidavit of purchase price all work, and the clerk uses them only to compute the tax. They are not recorded. If the transfer is exempt, the exemption has to appear on the face of the deed.

  • $100,000 sale: 200 units of $500, so $150.
  • $233,900 sale, the Census Bureau median home value: 468 units, so $351.
  • Under 68 O.S. 3201, the tax is limited to conveyances of realty that are sold.

How far back do McClain County land records go?

The OKCountyRecords index for McClain County shows data and scanned images from January 1980, with new records added in real time. The clerk's page says the office preserves property records dating back to the original U.S. land grants, so older records are held in the office even though the online index starts later.

Searches online can be run by name, book and page, instrument type, recording dates and legal description, including quarter, section, township and range. That is useful on rural McClain County land, where a deed may describe a quarter section instead of a lot and block.

Fees apply for printed copies on the online site, and the revenue goes to support the county. For a sale, pull the last vesting deed and any open mortgage releases before you list, so gaps in the chain show up early.

How did McClain County get its shape and history?

McClain County was created at statehood in 1907 and named for Charles M. McClain, who sat in the 1906 Constitutional Convention. Before then, the area was part of the Chickasaw Nation's Pontotoc County and had few settlers.

Railroads built the towns. The Southern Kansas Railway and the Gulf, Colorado and Santa Fe met at Purcell in 1886 and 1887, and the Oklahoma Central Railway of 1906 established Washington, Cole and Blanchard. Purcell was a starting point for the Land Run of 1889. The Purcell site notes it was founded in 1887 as a railroad town and is called the Quarter Horse Capital of the World.

Ranching came first, tied to Montford Johnson and others, and the county still ran about 50,000 head of cattle in 2000. Farming added corn, cotton, alfalfa and wheat over time.

What do McClain County numbers say about local housing?

The 2019 to 2023 Census Bureau survey counts 43,779 people and 17,125 housing units in McClain County. The median home value is $233,900, and median household income is $84,778.

MeasureMcClain County
People43,779
Housing units17,125
Median home value$233,900
Median household income$84,778
Owner-occupied78%

The state encyclopedia says the county's closeness to Oklahoma City and Norman has drawn commuters, and population rose from 27,740 in 2000 to 34,506 in 2010 and 41,667 in 2020. Interstate 35, Interstate 44 (the H. E. Bailey Turnpike, which ends in the county), and U.S. 62 and 77 cross the county. The Newcastle Bridge over the Canadian River, finished in 1913, gave county residents a direct route toward Oklahoma City.

What should McClain County sellers prepare before recording a deed?

Gather the signed and notarized deed, a closing statement or affidavit of purchase price, and a clear legal description. Then check the format, since a non-conforming page adds cost.

  1. Match the legal description to the last recorded deed.
  2. Prepare proof of the purchase price for the stamp tax.
  3. Check for any exemption and write it on the deed.
  4. Deliver the deed to 121 North 2nd Avenue in Purcell, or ask your title company to do so.
  5. Request a tax balance from the McClain County Treasurer, at 405-527-3261.

The treasurer's site says special assessments such as sewer, water, weed, cleaning, paving and nuisance abatement charges are certified to the treasurer after they become delinquent and are placed as a lien on the real estate account. The page we reviewed did not list due dates, so ask the office what applies to your account.

What do sellers in McClain County usually deal with?

Sellers in McClain County tend to hold either a commuter-town house near the Canadian River crossing or a rural tract with acreage. The stamp tax grows with the price, though the rate stays the same.

  • Inherited property where heirs live away from Purcell.
  • Land with mineral interests, which the clerk records separately.
  • Houses with lien or assessment questions.
  • Deeds that failed the format test and need to be redone.

More questions about McClain County, OK County Clerk

Where is the McClain County Clerk's office?

It is at 121 North 2nd Avenue in Purcell, with a mailing address of PO Box 629, Purcell, OK 73080. Land records can be reached at 405-527-3360, and the office is open from 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM.

What is the recording fee in McClain County?

The standard rate is $18.00 for the first page, made up of $8.00 for recording and $10.00 for preservation, plus $2.00 for each added page. Non-conforming documents cost $25.00 for the first page, $10.00 for each added page and a $10.00 preservation fee.

How is documentary stamp tax figured in McClain County?

The tax is $0.75 per $500 of the purchase price, rounded up, and applies when the price is above $100. Bring a closing statement, notarized bill of sale or affidavit of purchase price as proof of price.

Are McClain County land records online?

Yes. The OKCountyRecords site shows indexed data and scanned images from January 1980, and new records are added in real time. Printed copies carry fees.
